Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Transient stimulus, delayed re-challenge ('hornbook' priming test)
ideas.description: Expose cells to a brief stimulus (e.g., TPA, TNF, or injury signal), remove it, then re-stimulate after days to weeks and compare transcriptional responses to naive cells. Measure ATAC-seq, RNA-seq and FOS/JUN occupancy (CUT&RUN) to see whether AP-1-dependent primed or enhanced responses persist after the AP-1 protein levels return to baseline.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 degradation during the memory phase
ideas.description: Use dTAG/auxin-inducible degradation or a dominant-negative (A-FOS) to remove AP-1 either only during priming or only after priming, before re-challenge. If memory persists after AP-1 removal, AP-1 is only the initiator. If it is lost, AP-1 is needed to maintain the memory. Readouts are chromatin accessibility and the secondary response.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome tracking of chromatin and expression states
ideas.description: Run paired scATAC/scRNA-seq at multiple times after stimulation and after resting. Test whether AP-1 motif accessibility, AP-1 target expression and enhancer states are inherited by daughter cells, using lineage barcodes or sister-cell pairs to separate heritable memory from persistent signaling.

ideas.title: Enhancer-level epigenetic readout and engineered AP-1 sites
ideas.description: Map H3K27ac, H3K4me1, DNA methylation and nucleosome remodeling (BAF) at AP-1 bound enhancers before, after and long after stimulation. Then use dCas9 or motif mutation to delete or insert AP-1 sites at selected enhancers, to test whether binding is sufficient and necessary to leave a persistent open, primed state.

ideas.title: Live-cell reporters and mathematical modeling of feedback
ideas.description: Image endogenously tagged FOS/JUN and a downstream reporter in single cells during pulses of different duration and frequency. Fit bistable or positive-feedback models and test predictions, such as hysteresis and a threshold dose, by perturbing feedback loops (e.g., JUN autoregulation) to see if AP-1 dynamics alone can store state.
